a.statement: The continuum from instrument to environment is not a gradient of sophistication, but of invisibility — where the more deeply entangled the apparatus becomes, the less it is seen, yet the more it shapes the world through its silent, sedimented presence.

b.statement: The User/Tool dichotomy must be dismantled. Seamlessness masks the apparatus; entanglement is the material reality of human-machine coupling.
